text: I return to ordinary life with new capacity; calm becomes a flex.
I feel numb in a life that looks fine on paper.
I notice the ‘same house, same stress, same echo’ pattern and stop calling it normal.
I feel the ache of meaninglessness but keep performing so no one worries.
I numb out to survive, then resent the numbness.
I choose pain over numbness; sensation becomes a doorway back to myself.
I optimize myself for someone’s love and feel it turn uncanny.
I feel grief and keep moving forward.
I go looking for real feeling and end up borrowing suffering.
I step out of the row and risk looking strange to feel the truth.
I feel the discomfort that precedes change.
I stop asking what I should be and start meeting what I am.
I tolerate discomfort long enough for it to transform.
I cling to ordinary rules because wonder feels like losing control.
I want to stay a kid forever; responsibility feels like a trap.
I measure progress with outputs, not feelings.
Nothing behaves ‘properly’; I learn to adapt instead of argue.
I accept that freedom feels like fear at first.
I recognize that I am becoming reliable to myself.
I try the ‘no consequences’ life and discover indulgence still feels empty.
